Many years ago I got my first computer. It was a 286, later upgraded to a 386.
That was when I started learning programming.

After some time, when I became more confident, I upgraded it myself using my own money.
It became a Pentium MMX 233 system with a Voodoo3 3000 PCI and an Aureal Vortex2.
That machine contained my programs, experiments, documents, notes, and personal correspondence.

When I moved to another city, the computer stayed with my parents.
At some point they gave it away without asking me.
For them it was just an old, small, unremarkable machine.
For me it was something I had built and cared about.

I learned about it later, by accident.
That was probably the hardest hit I have experienced related to computers,
and it still feels unsettling to think about it.

Several years later, after some distance, I decided to start again from scratch
and bought a 486 system. I never had one before, so it was a new experience.

What surprised me was how difficult it had become to transfer files
between modern systems and a real DOS machine.
There are floppy disks and networking, but no USB, and practical FTP clients are missing.

FTP2P started as a way to solve that problem.
At the same time, it became a way to recreate the kind of software
I would have written back then, at that stage of my development.

Over the years I have received a lot from the computing world for free.
This project is a way to give something back.
